text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A20 do not appear at all (0 of 200 traces). In the later window each occurs at most once per trace: A14 in about 37 in 100 traces, A20 in about 34 in 100, and A15 in about 29 in 100. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- The three activities behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: in the later window, for each pair (for example A14 with A15, or A15 with A20) one or the other occurs in roughly 62–70 in 100 traces and neither in the remainder, and no trace contains both; in the earlier window neither member of any of these pairs was observed. [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- A36's routing changed: in the earlier window all of its observed outgoing transitions led to A21, while in the later window about 37 in 100 lead to A14, about 34 in 100 to A20, about 29 in 100 to A15, and only about 1 in 100 still go directly to A21. [DIR004]
- In the later window, every observed outgoing transition of A14, A15 and A20 leads to A21; in the earlier window these activities had no observed outgoing transitions because they did not occur. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- The ordering is consistent: in the later window A36 always precedes the new activity, and the new activity always precedes A21 (for example, A14 and A21 co-occur in about 37 in 100 traces, always with A14 first, and A14 and A36 co-occur in about 37 in 100 traces, always with A36 first). [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- The distance from A36 to A21 grew from one step in essentially all earlier traces to two steps in about 99 in 100 later traces, meaning exactly one activity now lies between them. [LAG001]
- The new activities sit at about one third of the trace (mean relative position about 0.35 in the later window), and A21, which occurs in every trace in both windows, now sits slightly later (mean relative position from about 0.37 to about 0.39). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: in the later window, a step was inserted between A36 and A21 — after A36, exactly one of three mutually exclusive activities (A14, A15 or A20) executes, and A21 follows it. In the earlier window A36 was followed directly by A21 in essentially all traces; in the later window a direct A36-to-A21 transition remains in only about 1 in 100 traces, the A36-to-A21 distance is two steps in about 99 in 100 traces, and each of the three inserted activities is taken in roughly 29–37 in 100 traces, always in the order A36, then the new activity, then A21. [DIR004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]

Supporting signs: 21 control-flow items qualified where fewer than 1 would be expected by chance among the 74 tested units, so the set of differences is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces, and each item's difference exceeds those seen in about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data. The placement is shown directly by the successor change at A36, the successors of the new activities, the lag change from one to two steps, and the relational evidence on exclusivity and order, rather than inferred from frequency shifts alone. [DIR004, LAG001, REL001, REL008]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window shows only that A14, A15 and A20 were not exercised there, so the evidence cannot rule out that these activities already existed but were rarely or never taken before; nor does it show how the choice among the three is made in a given trace. Several items describe the same underlying insertion, so they are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
